value.account:
Two defects, both only at 2.29+.
1) orchestrator/workflow/validation.py (_validate_repeat_until_on_exhausted): the 'may only override scalar repeat_until outputs' check ran before the exact-generated-ref check, so the compiler's own placeholder ref {"ref": root.steps.<loop>__exhausted_placeholders.artifacts.result__report} for a relpath field was rejected. I moved the generated-ref check first. It is still gated on allow_generated_repeat_until_on_exhausted_refs and requires the exact compiler-captured ref for that step/output, so hand-authored relpath overrides (literals or refs) are still rejected; a test covers that.
2) Fixing (1) exposed a runtime failure: on exhaustion the loop frame stores override values as unresolved {"ref":...} dicts, and the 2.29+ lowering (workflow_lisp/lowering/control_loops.py) made the result match join read those artifacts directly, failing with invalid_integer/invalid_relpath. This also affected scalar-only unions at 2.29 (e.g. :rounds state.round), independent of paths. Changes: (a) _loop_result_case_output_ref no longer disables the 2.28 behaviour of reading the exhausted variant's state-field refs directly from the loop state artifact at rich-loop targets; it now returns None when the state field is not a single flattened artifact (rich record/list fields), so those fall back as before. (b) new _exhausted_variant_placeholder_ref: in the exhausted variant's match case, inactive-variant fields that have a placeholder step are read from that step's artifact instead of the loop's ref-dict artifact.
Tests: tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_recur.py adds a parametrized compile+execute-to-exhaustion test for 2.28..2.32 (asserts variant UNRESOLVED and rounds 1 everywhere) and a negative test that a hand-authored relpath on_exhausted override stays rejected. The loop_recur, rich_loop_values and other loop modules pass (82 tests); the bugs/ repro dry-runs cleanly at 2.32.
Alternatives considered: dereferencing {"ref"} override values at runtime in repeat_until_exhaustion_artifacts (rejected: would change 2.28 artifacts, an existing test asserts the ref dict, and scope-qualified state keys for nested loops make ref parsing risky); relaxing the validator to accept any ref for relpath outputs (rejected as weakening validation); emitting a literal placeholder at 2.29+ like 2.28 (rejected: the placeholder-step design is deliberate for typed placeholders).
Not covered: I did not diff full compiled output byte-for-byte for 2.28 (existing byte-identity tests pass; 2.28 path is unchanged apart from the extra state-field existence check which only returns None for refs that would have dangled). Rich record/list state fields in on-exhausted at 2.29+ and nested/imported loops were not specifically exercised beyond existing tests. Pre-existing failures in test_workflow_lisp_key_migrations.py and test_workflow_lisp_phase_stdlib.py (17) are identical with and without my change. Full suite not run per instructions; nothing committed.
value.summary: Loop results with path fields in non-exhausted union variants now compile and exhaust identically at 2.29–2.32 as at 2.28, via a validator fix for compiler-emitted placeholder refs and a lowering fix so result matches read resolved values.

value.account:
Causa raíz (dos fallos, el segundo oculto tras el primero):
1) orchestrator/workflow_lisp/lowering/control_loops.py (_exhausted_inactive_placeholder_values): desde 2.29 se materializaba un placeholder para todo campo no escalar de variante inactiva, incluidos relpath; luego on_exhausted.outputs.result__report llevaba un ref y validation.py (_validate_repeat_until_on_exhausted) rechaza cualquier override relpath. Ahora los campos con kind relpath se excluyen del placeholder (kind not in {scalar, relpath}), con lo que se omiten del on_exhausted igual que en 2.28. La validación no se tocó.
2) orchestrator/workflow/loops.py (repeat_until_exhaustion_artifacts): una vez compilado, el agotamiento fallaba en runtime en 2.29+ (return__rounds = {"ref": ...} no era entero) porque desde 2.29 el join del match de resultado ya no lee el estado directamente (allow_exhaustion_state_ref=False) y los overrides de on_exhausted se guardaban como refs sin resolver. Esto ocurre también sin campos path (lo comprobé quitando el path). Ahora, solo con versión >= 2.29, un override que sea exactamente {"ref": "root.steps.<este loop>.artifacts.<n>"} se resuelve contra los artefactos del frame (ya ajustados al snapshot de estado del agotamiento). 2.28 y anteriores no cambian.
Tests: tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_result_paths.py ejecuta end-to-end (provider simulado) en 2.28–2.32: agotamiento -> UNRESOLVED con rounds correcto, camino done con APPROVE conserva el report, y salida de provider mal formada (report inexistente) sigue fallando. Pasan estos 15 y 116 tests de los módulos vecinos de loops/exhaustion/rich-loop/union-guards (1 xfail preexistente).
Alternativas descartadas: permitir en validation.py refs generados sobre relpath en on_exhausted (debilita la validación y el placeholder necesitaría un literal path que no existe); resolver {"ref"} genéricamente en _resolve_structured_output_artifacts (también habría aceptado salidas de provider con forma de ref, más laxo); reactivar allow_exhaustion_state_ref en 2.29+ (cambia el diseño de rich loop values).
No cubierto: refs a pasos placeholder (listas inactivas) siguen sin resolverse en el override, como antes, porque el materialize sigue la cadena de refs; campos path en variantes inactivas de uniones anidadas dentro de records se omiten en el agotamiento (antes se rechazaban, no probado en runtime); no ejecuté la suite completa ni hice commit.
value.summary: Un resultado de loop/recur con campo path en una variante no agotada ahora compila y se comporta igual en 2.29–2.32 que en 2.28 (dos cambios: lowering sin placeholder para relpath y resolución de refs de agotamiento en runtime).

value.account: Two defects. (1) orchestrator/workflow/validation.py _validate_repeat_until_on_exhausted: from 2.29 the compiler emits a ref to an __exhausted_placeholders step for a relpath loop output in an inactive variant, but the 'may only override scalar outputs' check ran before the generated-ref exemption. I moved the exemption first; it only matches the exact compiler-emitted ref when the generated-refs option is on, so authored relpath overrides (literal or ref) are still rejected (existing test_loader_validation coverage passes). (2) Once compiled, exhaustion failed at runtime at 2.29+: union result match joins read loop-frame artifacts without following {ref} values, so shared scalar fields (e.g. rounds = state.round) stayed as unresolved ref dicts and failed contract validation. At 2.28 the lowering read state fields directly. Fix in orchestrator/workflow/loops.py: new _resolve_exhaustion_override_refs resolves the compiler-emitted override refs to values when the exhausted frame is built (own-frame refs from the exhaustion snapshot, others via executor._resolve_ref_value), gated to >=2.29 so earlier targets are unchanged; unresolved refs raise LoopStateIntegrityError. Values still go through the join's validate_contract_value, and the malformed-path test still fails the run. Tests: tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_result_path_variants.py runs the bug's shape at 2.28-2.32 (compile, exhaustion, approve path, malformed path); 12 fail without the fix. Ran targeted modules only (loop exhaustion, rich loop values, loop_recur, loader_validation, strict boolean e2e, stdlib exhaustion): all pass. Considered and discarded: making the match/if join chain-follow ref dicts (broader, touches provider-fed values); lowering the exhaustion arm to read state directly at 2.29+ (would change rich-value lowering). Not covered: resume of a run interrupted mid-exhaustion on pre-fix state, nested loop-in-call scopes beyond root-ref resolution, and the full test suite (not run per instructions).
value.summary: Loop results with path fields in non-exhausted variants now compile and run identically at 2.29-2.32 as at 2.28, via a validator fix for generated exhaustion refs and runtime resolution of exhaustion override refs.

value.account:
Root cause: from 2.29 the compiler emits an `<loop>__exhausted_placeholders` materialize step and points on_exhausted.outputs.<relpath field> at it with a generated {"ref": ...}. (a) Shared validation rejected any relpath on_exhausted override before checking whether the ref was the exact compiler-generated one; (b) after that was fixed, the exhausted loop frame still held the raw {"ref"} dict, and the structured match join validated it as a relpath and failed with invalid_output_value. 2.28 simply omitted the field.
Changes: validation.py `_validate_repeat_until_on_exhausted` now runs the exact-generated-ref check before the relpath rejection (the check is only enabled for compiler lowering and matches the exact expected ref, so authored relpath overrides and arbitrary refs are still rejected; the existing loader test still passes). executor.py `_resolve_structured_output_artifacts` now follows a `{"ref": "root.steps...."}` stored by loop exhaustion via the new `_follow_loop_exhaustion_ref` and validates the resolved value against the unchanged output contract (a placeholder that is not a valid relpath would still fail). New tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_result_paths.py compiles and runs a union-result loop (exhausted, approved, escalated) at 2.28-2.32 with a patched provider execute and asserts workflow outputs equal the 2.28 outputs. Ran that module plus test_workflow_lisp_loop_recur.py, test_workflow_loops_exhaustion_state.py, test_loader_validation.py: all pass. Bug README command now gets past validation.
Considered and discarded: omitting the placeholder/relpath on_exhausted outputs at 2.29+ in control_loops.py (would match 2.28 output but the placeholder machinery was added deliberately for 2.29 inactive-arm normalization/resume, and changing lowering risks 2.29 artifacts); relaxing the validator to allow any relpath override (weakens validation); resolving refs generally in the executor (broader than needed), so I restricted the dereference to refs under root.steps.
Not covered: the full test suite was not run (only targeted modules); the dereference in the executor is keyed on the ref shape rather than on a flag that the value came from on_exhausted, so a stored artifact dict of exactly {"ref": "root.steps..."} would also be followed there; resume-from-checkpoint after exhaustion and imported-workflow loops were not exercised; the repo CLAUDE.md asks for Spanish replies but this result is in English as the task was written in English; nothing under bugs/ was edited and nothing committed.
value.summary: Loop results with a path field in an inactive variant now compile and run identically at targets 2.29-2.32 as at 2.28, via two small changes in orchestrator/workflow (validation.py, executor.py) plus a regression test.
